_comment: Expected panel output for the F2 calibration set. Every entry is an ARBITER-SETTLED answer, not a guess — each cites the ruling that settled it. 'must' = the slug has to appear; 'must_not' = it must not; 'flag' = a flags entry is expected instead of a tag. Slugs not named are unconstrained: these papers were never adjudicated against the other new vocabulary, so silence there is neither right nor wrong and is not scored.
_scoring: A definition FAILS calibration if a must is missed or a must_not fires at >=2/3 vendor agreement. A single dissenting vendor is noise; a majority is a definition that reads wrong.

GAD5Z8PV.author: Vargas
GAD5Z8PV.why: §147b. 'a static orchestration model with three fixed phases'; 'orchestrator with fixed prompts, which prevents early' termination. Deterministic orchestration with AI verdicts — the Q2-yes/Q1-no cell. If rules-based-checks-v2 fires here, the panel is conflating orchestration with checking, which is the exact error the facet was coined to prevent.

UB2EVUFU.author: Lyu
UB2EVUFU.why: §147b, the MIXED case and the hardest positive. Phase transitions in code — 'the orchestrator does not make software engineering decisions itself' — while manager agents 'dynamically hire, assign' the team. Tests whether the panel asks about CONTROL FLOW rather than whether any model has discretion anywhere. A miss here means precondition 1 is being over-applied.

72W6R4JG.author: Töpfer
72W6R4JG.why: §139a positive — FCL constraint verifier, verdict computed. And the reverse dissociation: essentially no orchestration machinery and no agent discretion to constrain, so precondition 2 of §147b fails.

3SU9QZ6F.author: Parris
3SU9QZ6F.why: §139a positive — AIRA, 15 deterministic checks. Same dissociation as Töpfer. These two are why the two slugs are separate rather than merged.

UDVHQ5HR.author: Jin
UDVHQ5HR.why: §147a + §148b. THE HYBRID and the curation ruling, on the JOURNAL text (§148a — the corpus text was the preprint until 2026-08-29 and contained neither the filter nor the 88.74% figure). rules-based-checks-v2 must NOT fire: the Fix-guided Verification Filter executes deterministically but over GPT-4o-generated tests, so the verdict is not independent of a model's judgement — §139a's third conjunct. A CENSUS flag is required anyway so the hybrid class can be counted. evaluated-synthetic MUST fire per §148b: the authors curated AND MODIFIED HumanEval/MBPP/QuixBugs tasks into paired conforming/non-conforming variants — created instances, not selected ones — and 'concocting a dataset from established datasets is still synthetic'.

7UB2MD8Z.author: Kang
7UB2MD8Z.why: §121b positive — '70% agreed' explanations were wanted; a stated preference about tooling, reported as a result. This is the case that defeated the centrality reading twice (§121b, §145a), so a miss here means centrality has crept back in.

T72TU8B5.author: Shukla
T72TU8B5.why: §145a — the NEW third condition, and the only paper that tests it in isolation. The N=21 survey passes the instrument test AND the elicitation test ('evolving preferences for level of oversight') but is FORMATIVE: it motivates the design rather than reporting a finding. If this fires, the reported-vs-formative test is not being applied.

B644HQFS.author: Baltes
B644HQFS.why: §116a — no instrument at all. 1,154 mined Reddit/HN posts, nobody surveyed. The precondition that survives every version of the definition.

A6ZE2A26.author: Ullah
A6ZE2A26.why: §140a — the reference case for the two architecture facets. Unanimous committees of 1–6 judges ruling on the SAME query (a vote is lost, not a job), composed of DISTINCT models with composition measured as a variable, and the paper's subject is the reliability of those juries. Also checks the §146a namespace fix: evaluator-reliability must arrive as a THEME.
